title: Typed stream failure modes and operator playbook for deferred tool handoffs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define unambiguous acceptance criteria for streamed structured outputs that trigger deferred tool/function calls, enumerate failure classes for partial emits, and provide an operator playbook for safe recovery and customer-facing remediation. This ticket captures the PM-level requirements and acceptance criteria. Engineering will implement protocol changes (frame markers, commit points, idempotency tokens) and telemetry hooks; Design/DevEx may supply sample SDK helpers for clients to resume or reconcile partial state.
background: Motivation: production incidents in Q4 2025 and Jan 2026 showed two recurring failure patterns: (1) partial JSON-like fragments emitted before a tool call failed and could not be reconciled by downstream systems, and (2) ambiguous tool-invoke retries caused duplicate side effects. Existing docs cover schema evolution and progressive envelopes, but operators lacked a concise runbook tying failure class to immediate mitigation and customer communication. This PRD consolidates acceptance criteria, telemetry, and operator steps to reduce MTTR and avoid unsafe retries.
scope_changes: In scope: definition of failure modes for typed streaming frames, acceptance criteria for idempotent tool-handshake semantics, required telemetry/events, operator runbook steps, test cases, and rollout guidance. Out of scope: changes to persistence layer or long-term retention of tool invocation logs (handled by ENG-22111) and per-customer consent flows for resending actions.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: Every top-level streamed frame must include a frame_version, frame_id (UUID), emit_type (partial|commit|abort), and optional tool_handshake object with tool_id and idempotency_token. All new fields must be backward-compatible with v1 clients.

Partial vs Commit semantics: A 'partial' emit can be followed by zero or more 'partial' frames and must be followed by either a 'commit' frame (finalization) or an 'abort' frame within 30s for real-time routes; if neither arrive within configured timeout, runtime must emit a 'emit.timed_out' event and mark the stream state as 'stalled'.

Tool handshake: When the runtime signals a deferred tool invocation, it must emit 'tool.invoke.start' with tool_id and idempotency_token and only deliver 'tool.invoke.complete' once external tool confirms success. If the tool returns a transient error, the runtime must follow exponential backoff and not emit duplicate 'commit' frames without explicitly incrementing retry_count in telemetry.

Idempotency: Tool backends must be invoked with an idempotency_token that is stable for the logical operation; acceptance tests must prove that replaying the same token results in at-most-once side effects for repairable and terminal error classifications.

Error classification: The runtime must classify errors into 'transient' (retryable), 'repairable' (requires operator or client intervention to rehydrate state), and 'terminal' (must abort stream). Tests must show deterministic classification for a representative set of external tool HTTP 4xx/5xx and network timeouts.

Observability: For every stream, the runtime must emit events: emit.partial, emit.commit, emit.abort, emit.timed_out, tool.invoke.start, tool.invoke.retry, tool.invoke.complete, tool.invoke.failed. These must include frame_id, session_id, route, model, and latency_ms. Acceptance requires dashboards and an alert rule that fires on >0.5% stalled streams in a 5m window for production routes.

Client SDK behavior: SDKs should expose a resume() helper that accepts the last-seen frame_id and idempotency_token and reconcilers must be able to request a reflection endpoint to obtain final commit/abort status; acceptance requires a sample integration test confirming resume() recovers deterministic final state in 3 simulated failure scenarios.
Streaming backward compatibility: v1 clients (no frame metadata) must continue to receive full responses for non-streamed routes. Feature flag must gate v2 frames on new routes until canary passes.

Security: idempotency_token must be treated as a secret with limited lifetime; logs must not contain raw tokens beyond ephemeral debug traces. Acceptance requires code paths that redact tokens in standard logs and keep token visibility to 'debug' only behind a flag.
Performance: Added frame metadata must not increase median latency by more than 3% on real-time routes under typical load (measured at 95th percentile over a 1h synthetic workload).
test_plan: Automated: unit tests for encoder/decoder to assert frame envelope correctness; integration tests that simulate (A) tool success, (B) transient tool failures with automatic retry, (C) repairable error that requires operator resume, (D) network partition and stream timeout. Each must validate emitted telemetry events and final output reconciliation. Manual: run canary with 5% traffic for 48h against a synthetic consumer that validates idempotency and duplicate side-effect detection. Post-canary soak test for 7 days on dedicated capacity. Test artifacts: JSON test vectors and a GitHub Actions workflow under /ci/streaming-v2.
rollout_notes: Rollout should use feature flag 'streaming_v2_frames' with staged gate: dev -> staging (smoke) -> canary (5%) -> canary (25%) -> global. During canary, enable verbose telemetry for 1h windows then revert to sampling. If stalled_stream alert triggers >3x baseline during canary, auto-roll back. Coordinate with Customer Success for any customers on Dedicated to opt-in. Communicate to SDK teams two weeks prior to enablement.
telemetry: Required metrics/events: metric.emit_partial_count, metric.emit_commit_count, metric.emit_abort_count, metric.emit_timed_out_count, metric.tool_invoke_start_count, metric.tool_invoke_retry_count, metric.tool_invoke_success_count, metric.tool_invoke_failure_count. Traces must include frame_id, parent_request_id, route, model, worker_id, and timings for tool roundtrip. Logs must include structured reason codes for failures (e.g., TOOL_HTTP_502, TOOL_TIMEOUT, FRAME_PARSE_ERROR).
operator_playbook: Detection: Alert 'stalled_stream' surfaces for a route. Use Observability dashboard 'Streaming v2 — Stalled Streams' to identify affected session_ids and frame_ids.

Quick triage: Check tool.invoke.* event rates. If tool.invoke.retry_count is increasing and tool_invoke_success_count remains zero, mark incident as TOOL_BACKEND_DEGRADED and escalate to Backend Tooling owner.

Customer mitigation: If >10% of a single customer's streams are stalled, toggle feature flag off for that customer and initiate graceful aborts for active sessions. Notify CS with template message and recommended remediation steps.

Repair flow: For repairable errors, run reconcilier script with last_committed_frame_id and idempotency_token to replay safely; if unknown state, use reflect endpoint to fetch authoritative state and instruct client SDK to resume with resume(frame_id).

Abort/rollback: For terminal errors or repeated retries beyond threshold, emit an automated abort frame on behalf of the model with reason code and surface user-facing error consistent with platform error schema.

Post-incident: Collect sample stream traces and attach to incident ticket; run RCA to update classification heuristics and tests. If caused by ambiguous idempotency token generation, schedule follow-up to rotate token provenance and update SDKs.
Communication: Use templated public and private messages. For high-severity events affecting SLAs, include timeline, customer impact, and remediation steps within 2 hours.
Escalation: If operator cannot determine safe repair within 30 minutes for high-impact customer, escalate to on-call Engineering runtime owner and Product manager.
notes: Decision logs: prefer explicit commit/abort frames over inferring end-of-stream from idle gaps to avoid duplicate-tool-invokes. We will allocate an opt-in canary in dedicated clusters first. SDK resume helpers will be implemented in TypeScript and Python; other languages can reuse REST reflection endpoint. Consider future work: cryptographically signed commit frames for cross-service trust.

Run at-most-once side-effect experiment for idempotency tokens
Ensure logs redact idempotency_token in non-debug levels
Smoke test client SDK resume() flow with simulated commit/abort races
Verify alert thresholds and dashboard tiles appear in staging
